iconicAnchor.label: Caravaggio's dramatic tenebrism
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Michelangelo Merisi da Caravaggio and seventeenth-century followers
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: Caravaggio's compressed incidents, ordinary bodies, hard directional light, and engulfing dark establish the style's dramatic mechanism rather than merely a dark palette.

sources.title: Caravaggio and His Followers
supports: Caravaggio's influence depended on forceful naturalism, figures brought close to the viewer, and dramatic contrasts of illumination and shadow.

sources.title: Caravaggio: Darkness at Noon
supports: Chiaroscuro functions compositionally by selecting decisive faces, hands, and objects from darkness rather than evenly modeling an entire scene.
